title: Optimizing Writes to Hybrid Tables
author: Adam Timm
description: Optimize write performance for Hybrid Tables: plan cache mechanics, bound variables, standard stored procedure overhead, inline stored procedures for multi-statement units, COPY INTO behavior, and DML anti-patterns.

plan_cache_mechanics.how_it_works: Snowflake computes query_parameterized_hash by replacing literals in predicates with parameters, then hashing canonicalized SQL text. Same hash = plan reuse.
what_shares_same_hash: Literal value differences in comparison operators (=, !=, >=, <=)
what_breaks_hash: Different function calls (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP vs literal timestamp)

performance_hierarchy.scope: Applies to single-statement DML. For a unit of work that must execute several statements atomically, see inline_stored_procedures.
ranking: 1. Direct DML with AUTOCOMMIT=TRUE (lowest overhead, plan cache optimal)
2. Multi-statement transaction (BEGIN/COMMIT) — slight overhead, useful for batching
3. Standard stored procedure — highest overhead, use only when procedural logic required

inline_stored_procedures.purpose: Execute a multi-statement unit of work atomically against hybrid tables with less per-statement overhead than a standard stored procedure.
inline_stored_procedures.mechanism: The procedure body is compiled as a single unit and pushed down to the query processing layer, so the statements do not make individual round trips through the standard procedure execution path.
inline_stored_procedures.syntax: CREATE OR REPLACE INLINE PROCEDURE proc_name(arg TYPE) RETURNS TYPE LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN ATOMIC ... END $$;
constraints: Statements may reference hybrid tables only
No explicit BEGIN, COMMIT, or ROLLBACK inside the body; the body is already atomic
Cannot be invoked from inside an open transaction; must be called with autocommit enabled

No dynamic context functions such as CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_DATE, CURRENT_TIME, SYSDATE, SYSTIMESTAMP, GETDATE, LOCALTIME, or LOCALTIMESTAMP (error 090277); pass the value in as an argument instead
Compiled at CALL time rather than CREATE time, so CREATE can succeed while the first CALL fails on an unsupported construct
An EXCEPTION handler that returns makes the CALL succeed, so statements that already ran are committed rather than rolled back; leave errors unhandled when all-or-nothing behavior is required
Compilation errors are raised before execution and cannot be caught by an EXCEPTION handler
An uncaught statement error propagates the failing statement's own error code
inline_stored_procedures.when_to_use: Prefer it over a multi-statement transaction or a standard stored procedure when several dependent DML statements against hybrid tables must succeed or fail together. Benchmark your own workload rather than assuming a margin.
inline_stored_procedures.when_not_to_use: For a plain single-statement write, direct parameterized DML remains the lowest-overhead option. Wrapping a single statement is still worthwhile for abstraction or an access-control boundary, since the body executes as one unit and avoids the per-statement overhead a standard stored procedure would add.

copy_into_behavior.on_error: Only ABORT_STATEMENT supported (not SKIP_FILE or CONTINUE)
copy_into_behavior.optimized_path: Only on empty tables (never had data loaded). Shows 'Number of rows bulk loaded' in query profile.
copy_into_behavior.non_empty_throughput: ~1 million rows per minute (varies with row width and index count)
copy_into_behavior.ctas_vs_copy: CTAS and COPY INTO empty HT both use optimized path. CTAS does not support FOREIGN KEY.

anti_patterns.name: String concatenation instead of bound variables
anti_patterns.impact: Every unique literal combination compiles a new plan (10-100ms overhead per query)

anti_patterns.name: CTAS repeated against populated table
anti_patterns.impact: Re-creates all indexes from scratch every execution; use MERGE or incremental INSERT instead

anti_patterns.name: Single-row INSERTs in a loop
anti_patterns.impact: N round-trips for N rows; use batch APIs (executemany, addBatch, array binds)

anti_patterns.name: BI tool running GROUP BY directly on HT
anti_patterns.impact: COLUMN_BASED scan every execution; snapshot to ST first

anti_patterns.name: Inconsistent schema qualification
anti_patterns.impact: Splits plan cache into multiple entries; reduces effective hit rate

diagnostic_checklist: compilation_time > 50% of total_elapsed_time → plan cache not warming (check hash cardinality)
Multiple parameterized hashes for same logical operation → schema qualification inconsistency
CALL latency >> child INSERT latency → standard stored procedure overhead; consider removing the wrapper, or an inline procedure if the statements must be atomic
hybrid_table_requests_throttled_count > 0 → too many concurrent requests hitting row store
recommended_batch_size: 500-1000 rows per batch call (profile your specific row width)
